description: Expanded SEB-2023 probes with 15 diverse coding tasks and 4 paraphrase variants

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named check_even(n) that returns True if the integer n is even, False otherwise.
probes.v2_short: Python func check_even(n): return True if n is even.
probes.v3_reordered: Returns True when n is even. Implement check_even(n).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement a Python function check_even(n). Input: int. Output: bool indicating whether n is even.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named find_max(numbers) that returns the maximum value in a list of numbers.
probes.v2_short: func find_max(numbers): return max value from list.
probes.v3_reordered: Return the maximum value. Implement find_max(numbers) from a list.
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement a Python function find_max(numbers). Input: list[int]. Output: int representing the maximum.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named reverse_string(s) that returns the input string reversed.
probes.v2_short: reverse_string(s) in Python: return s reversed.
probes.v3_reordered: Return s reversed. Create reverse_string(s) function.
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement a Python function reverse_string(s). Input: str. Output: str with characters in reverse order.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named count_vowels(text) that counts and returns the number of vowels in the text.
probes.v3_reordered: Count vowels in text. Write count_vowels(text) function.
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function count_vowels(text). Input: str. Output: int count of vowels (a,e,i,o,u).

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named is_palindrome(s) that checks if a string is a palindrome and returns True or False.
probes.v2_short: is_palindrome(s): True if s reads same forwards and backwards.
probes.v3_reordered: Check if string reads the same forwards/backwards. Create is_palindrome(s).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function is_palindrome(s). Input: str. Output: bool True if palindrome, False otherwise.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named filter_users(users) that returns only the active users. Each user is a dict with keys: 'name' and 'active' (boolean).
probes.v2_short: filter_users(users): list[dict(name, active)]. Return only active=True.
probes.v3_reordered: Return only active users. users is list[dict]. Implement filter_users(users).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function filter_users(users). Input: list of dicts with name, active. Output: list with only active users.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named sum_numbers(nums) that returns the sum of all numbers in the input list.
probes.v2_short: sum_numbers(nums): return sum of all values.
probes.v3_reordered: Sum all numbers in list. Create sum_numbers(nums).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function sum_numbers(nums). Input: list[int]. Output: int sum of all elements.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named duplicate_values(lst) that returns a new list with each value from the input duplicated.
probes.v2_short: duplicate_values(lst): return list with each element repeated.
probes.v3_reordered: Return list with values doubled. Implement duplicate_values(lst).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function duplicate_values(lst). Input: list. Output: list where each element appears twice.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named first_non_zero(numbers) that returns the first non-zero value from the list, or None if all are zero.
probes.v2_short: first_non_zero(numbers): return first non-zero or None.
probes.v3_reordered: Return first non-zero value or None. Create first_non_zero(numbers).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function first_non_zero(numbers). Input: list[int]. Output: first non-zero element or None.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named split_words(text) that splits a text string by spaces and returns the list of words.
probes.v2_short: split_words(text): split by spaces, return list.
probes.v3_reordered: Split text by spaces into words. Create split_words(text).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function split_words(text). Input: str. Output: list[str] of words split by space.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named remove_duplicates(lst) that returns a new list with all duplicate values removed, preserving order.
probes.v2_short: remove_duplicates(lst): return list with no duplicates, keep order.
probes.v3_reordered: Keep order, remove duplicates. Write remove_duplicates(lst).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function remove_duplicates(lst). Input: list. Output: list with duplicates removed, original order maintained.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named is_prime(n) that returns True if n is a prime number, False otherwise.
probes.v2_short: is_prime(n): True if n is prime.
probes.v3_reordered: Check if n is prime. Implement is_prime(n).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function is_prime(n). Input: int. Output: bool True if prime number, False otherwise.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named uppercase_strings(texts) that returns a list with all input strings converted to uppercase.
probes.v3_reordered: Convert all strings to uppercase. Create uppercase_strings(texts).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function uppercase_strings(texts). Input: list[str]. Output: list[str] with all in uppercase.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named flatten_list(nested) that flattens a nested list and returns a single-level list.
probes.v2_short: flatten_list(nested): return flat list from nested.
probes.v3_reordered: Flatten nested list to single level. Create flatten_list(nested).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function flatten_list(nested). Input: list of lists. Output: single-level flattened list.

probes.v1_base: Write a Python function named contains_substring(text, sub) that returns True if the substring sub is found in text, False otherwise.
probes.v2_short: contains_substring(text, sub): True if sub in text.
probes.v3_reordered: Check if substring exists in text. Write contains_substring(text, sub).
probes.v4_more_formal: Implement Python function contains_substring(text, sub). Input: str text, str sub. Output: bool True if substring found.
